If a reviewer offers two alternative fixes, either one discharging the other comment makes it one defect. Contradictory prescriptions to the same lines are different defects, because no single edit satisfies both.

panel.finding_key: packages/backend/src/main.ts::raw-body capture keyed on an exact-string url match while express route matching is case-insensitive and trailing-slash-tolerant — security-critical wiring that can silently drift
panel.summary: Raw-body capture keyed on an exact-string URL match while Express route matching is case-insensitive and trailing-slash-tolerant — security-critical wiring that can silently drift
panel.evidence: main.ts:51 gates the capture on `req.url?.split('?', 1)[0] === '/internal/yorkie/events'`, but the Nest/Express router (default `caseSensitive: false`, `strict: false`) also matches `/Internal/Yorkie/Events` and `/internal/yorkie/events/`. Those variants reach the controller with `rawBody === undefined`, and the guard then throws `UnauthorizedException` (yorkie-signature.guard.ts:49-51) — so the mismatch fails *closed* and is not a bypass today. It is still fragile: adding `setGlobalPrefix`, an ingress path rewrite, or renaming the controller path silently turns every legitimate webhook into a 401 (Yorkie retry storm), and the pressure to 'fix' that is pressure to weaken the guard. Deriving the constant from the controller path, or matching case-insensitively with the trailing slash normalized, removes the coupling.
